Voicemeeter ignores Windows channel volu: Voicemeeter ignores Windows channel volume, so for Voicemeeter output devices each speaker's level is set in the bus EQ of the bus you pick, using cells 5 and 6 of that speaker's channel as a flat volume control. Voicemeeter keeps these with its own settings, so they stay applied whether or not Daisy's App is running. Needs Voicemeeter Banana or Potato; the range is ±12 dB.
Pick the bus under Output device on the: Pick the bus under Output device on the Audio Tools tab. Turning this off leaves any levels already in Voicemeeter as they are; use Reset levels first if you want them cleared.
On the Audio Tools tab, drag a speaker t: On the Audio Tools tab, drag a speaker to any cell to match where it is in your room; dropping it on another speaker swaps them. Positions are saved for each output device. With an odd grid size the middle cell is the listener's.
The test signal, subwoofer low-pass and: The test signal, subwoofer low-pass and auto-cycle options are on the Audio Tools tab, next to the speaker map. They're saved as you change them. Auto-level always uses band-limited pink noise.
Voicemeeter ignores Windows channel volu: Voicemeeter ignores Windows channel volume and its Remote API wasn't found, so the level knobs won't change what you hear on this device.

Noise sent to the LFE channel is band-li: Noise sent to the LFE channel is band-limited to the subwoofer range, as in standard calibration.
Low-pass corner frequency for the subwoo: Low-pass corner frequency for the subwoofer test signal (24 dB/octave). 80 Hz is the common crossover.
Plays at −20 dBFS RMS, the calibration s: Plays at −20 dBFS RMS, the calibration standard. With an SPL meter, set each speaker to 75 dB SPL (C-weighted, slow). Turn off Spatial sound and audio enhancements for the device.
